assessment: Two baskets remove the separate Mouser and Coilcraft freight without forcing a new controller, additional protection IC, larger transformer, parallel output-capacitor bank or lower-voltage replacement for R7.

Retaining L1, R7 and C6 avoids unnecessary magnetic, high-voltage-resistor and output-capacitor qualification changes. RF1 changes value within the existing Bourns fusible family and same footprint to damp the modeled input transient, rather than adding a separate fuse/resistor network.

T1 is a manufacturer-supported HV energy inductor in the consolidated DigiKey order. Its move and the resulting local reroute are justified by the manufacturer-sensitive-traces-under-body guidance. The increased track count is not by itself evidence of needless complexity.

C1 higher voltage and pulse rating address the new input-voltage screen; lower initial dV/dt after RF1=47 ohm does not justify a smaller 630 V candidate when the modeled C1 peak is approximately 706 V.
D1 to a 1000 V part in the same package is a proportionate margin improvement after the modeled filtered bus approached the old 600 V rating. It adds no positions or routing function.

R6's 100-piece minimum costs more than one fitted resistor but is included honestly in the one-build purchase budget. No additional series/parallel sensing network is introduced merely to use standard values.

The user's preference for TME is satisfied pragmatically rather than interpreted as a requirement to buy every part there. C5 remains a single original DigiKey part, avoiding the more expensive TME minimum of ten pieces.
